title: Autonomic Admin Bridgelet and Runstate Harmonizer
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a small, hardened service ("bridgelet") that exposes safe admin utilities as first-class, idempotent tasks and a complementary Runstate Harmonizer that converts free-form runbook steps into structured task state. The goal is to let support engineers run verified remediation actions (and rollbacks) with telemetry, explicit checkpoints, and automatic fallbacks when preconditions aren't met. This is aimed at reducing on-call cognitive load, eliminating shell-based one-offs, and improving reproducibility of incident remediations.
background: We have several one-off admin scripts and ad-hoc runbook steps that are brittle: manual shell commands, fragile sequence dependencies, and weak telemetry. Incidents reveal repeated mistakes and risky manual fixes. This project wraps common utilities (restarts, cache clears, config bakes, model fallback toggles) in a small RPC surface that enforces pre-checks, idempotency, and structured audit trails. The Runstate Harmonizer takes runbook text / previous incident transcripts and maps them to a sequence of harmonized tasks with required invariants and checkpoint hooks.
design_decisions: Expose a narrow RPC API: executeTask(task_id, params) and queryTask(task_id) to make automation composable and auditable.
Persist task state as append-only events in Postgres + JSON payloads (event rows are simple strings) to aid replay and audits rather than a complex event store.
Each task must declare preconditions, idempotency key, timeout, and a compensating rollback action.
Use optimistic concurrency (+ sequence version) for task transitions to avoid global locks; fall back to advisory locks for multi-resource ops.
Ship with a whitelist of safe primitives; new primitives require a small safety checklist and owner approval before enabling in prod.
Telemetry: emit structured metrics for task.duration.p95, task.failure_rate, task.manual_escalation_count and link to existing dashboards.
Runstate Harmonizer will be a thin transformation layer (heuristics + small rule set) to propose task sequences; final edits required by oncall/engineer before execution.
Rollouts will be gated behind feature flags (console-ops-bridgelet) and a canary group of SREs.
Prefer small binary (Go) with minimal dependencies for security and fast startup in Dedicated/Private environments.
Avoid shipping secret management; integrate with KMS/HSM via existing infra connectors rather than in-process key handling.
tradeoffs: Choosing Postgres append-only events simplifies operations and backups but sacrifices high-throughput event streaming semantics.
Whitelist of primitives reduces agility for emergent fixes; mitigated by a documented fast-track review process.
Optimistic concurrency avoids heavy locking but requires careful retry semantics in clients.
Runstate Harmonizer will not be fully ML-driven initially — we prioritize deterministic rules to keep behavior auditable.
Shipping as a small service increases operational surface vs. embedding in existing operator tooling, but improves boundary clarity and rollout control.
acceptance_criteria: Bridgelet can register and execute at least 12 approved primitive actions with idempotency preserved across retries.
Every executed task writes an audit event and emits telemetry to the ops metrics cluster (visible in dashboard link below).
Runstate Harmonizer can convert a canonical incident runbook into a proposed task sequence with editable checkpoints.
SRE can run a canary plan and observe p95 latency < 200ms for the happy path execution of primitives under normal load.
Feature flagged and rolled out to a small SRE group with documented enable/disable steps and rollback plan.
implementation_notes: PR template must include safety checklist and owner sign-off for any new primitive added.
Integration targets: Console UI (actions panel), Oncall Slack shortcuts, and Runbook editor export.
Schema: tasks table (id, key, status, seq, payload, created_at, updated_at) stored as flat columns; payload is JSON string.
Testing: end-to-end harness that replays 10 historical incident traces and verifies identical post-condition states.
CI: static analysis, small fuzz tests for input params, and a safety smoke job that runs in staging daily.
risks: A buggy primitive could cause cascading failures if preconditions are insufficient — mitigated by rollout flags and auto-mitigations (circuit-breaker).
Misclassification by the Harmonizer may propose unsafe sequences; require human validation step before execution.
Telemetry gaps could hide regressions; include a strict QA checklist requiring metric presence before enabling a primitive.
Performance under contention (many parallel tasks touching same resources) needs conservative retries to avoid hammering services.
